chunks: As for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), we say that God must protect him so that he may deliver the religious laws, because it is not possible to know that except through him; therefore, protection from him is obligatory.

The Imam is not like him, because the excuse of the obligated ones is removed regarding the religious laws, and the proofs are established for what they need, and they have a way to know them without his words,

and if we suppose that the situation reaches a point where the truth among the religious duties is not known except through his words, then it would be necessary for God Almighty to protect him and manifest him in such a way that no harm can reach him, as in the case of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

The like of the case of the Imam is that when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) has delivered [the message] and then what follows presents something that causes fear, it is not necessary for God to protect him from being prevented, because the excuse of the obligated ones has been removed by what he delivered to them, so they have a way to know His grace.

Unless there is another delivery attached to him in the future, then protection from him is obligatory as it was obligatory at the beginning; thus we have equated the matter between the Prophet and the Imam.

key_terms.الْمُكَلَّفِينَ: The obligated ones (believers subject to divine law)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in the obligation of divine protection between the Prophet and the Imam according to Tusi?
ai.summary: Tusi distinguishes the Prophet’s divine protection as an absolute necessity for the initial delivery of the Shariah, whereas the Imam’s protection is contingent upon the community's ongoing need for his authoritative interpretation to resolve ambiguity. This nuanced view underscores the Imam’s role as the living interpreter of revelation, ensuring that the 'cause of the worshippers' remains satisfied through accessible guidance. By equating the two in cases of future necessity, Tusi reinforces the continuity of divine authority and the Imam’s essential role in preserving the integrity of Islamic law.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: As for the Prophet (s), we say that God must protect him so he may deliver religious laws, because it is not possible to discern religious laws, except through him.

However, the Imam is not like him, because as far as the delivery of religious laws is concerned, the public does not have any excuse  and all rules they need are indicated by their proofs and it is possible for them to learn them without needing Imam’s words.

If we suppose that religious duties cannot be known, except through the words of the Imam, then it will be necessary that God Almighty should protect him and manifest him in such a way that no harm can reach him, as in the case of the Messenger (a.s).

The like of the case of the Imam is that once a prophet has delivered the message and then his security is threatened, it is not necessary for God to protect him, because the excuse of the public has been removed through his delivery and they have a path to discern the grace imposed upon them.

However, it is possible that there might be another message that must be delivered in the future, which may require God to protect him as He protected him in the beginning. Thus we equated the matter between the Prophet and the Imam.
